I haven't implemented issue #33 yet. No code is written, nothing is committed or pushed, and there's no PR.

**What I actually did:**
- Created a local branch `feat/33-worktree-continuity`. It has no commits and isn't pushed.
- Installed the dev dependencies with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. The checkout only had production dependencies, so `vitest` was missing. On a clean `main` the suite passes: 25 files, 302 tests.
- Read the code the feature touches: `src/thread.ts`, `src/push.ts`, the storage modules, `src/run.ts`, `src/answers.ts`, `src/github-ui.ts`, `action.yml`, README and CONTRIBUTING. I also read the pi-durable API for conversation documents, forks and hooks.

**Design decisions I reached (none of them in code yet):**
- **When the pointer is visible to a fork.** A fork sees a document's value as of the commit that holds the fork entry. Writing the snapshot pointer in a separate commit after a turn would leave forks one step behind. So each snapshot would write the pointer document and append a model-invisible `pi-action.worktree` entry in one commit. A fork at that entry or later then sees the snapshot.
- **Hooks can't do it.** pi-durable hooks are read-only, so they can't write the document.
- **Atomic push.** `GitSync` needs an optional second ref so `refs/pi/threads/<n>` and `refs/pi/worktrees/<n>` go out in one `git push --atomic`.
- **Final push step.** `src/push.ts` would have to open the thread's storage and conversation, without restarting interrupted work, to take a last snapshot and record its pointer.
- **Guard question.** Its answer has to be consumed at restore time, before the model gets it.
- **After a restore.** Restoring an older snapshot needs a new wrapper commit on top of the ref. Otherwise the next run sees target ≠ latest and asks the same question again.

**Problems still to solve:**
- **Shallow checkouts.** `actions/checkout` clones with depth 1, so checking whether the remote branch moved ahead of the recorded `Head` needs the history deepened first.
- **Read-only tokens.** Apart from fork PRs, I see no reliable way to detect them up front. The plan was to rely on the push failing.
- **When the guard matters.** pi-action never forks or rewinds the root conversation today. The guard would only trigger when a pointer write failed, or after a future rewind feature.

**Open questions:** none of them block. The plan was to use the proposed defaults (10 MB per file, 100 MB per snapshot, the `.env*`/`*.pem`/`*.key`/`id_rsa*` denylist) and keep the snapshot document visible to the action only, then say so in the PR.

**Still to do:** everything in the acceptance criteria. That means `src/storage/worktree.ts` and its tests, the lifecycle wiring in `src/thread.ts`, `src/push.ts` and `src/run.ts`, the new inputs in `action.yml` and `src/inputs.ts`, the README and CONTRIBUTING sections, focused commits, the push, and the PR. Because nothing is committed, nothing from this session survives the end of the run except what's written here.
